name: Energy Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public energy data.

entries.title: EIA-860 Annual Electric Generator Report
entries.description: Generator-level data on every existing and planned U.S. electric generating unit of 1 MW or more — location, capacity, technology, fuel, and status — collected through Form EIA-860.
entries.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. Page shows "Release Date: September 10, 2026, Final 2025 data" with an early release of 2026 data due June 2027. The 1 MW threshold and the 1990 start year come from EIA's usual description of the survey and should be confirmed by a steward. EIA publications are public domain (EIA Copyrights and Reuse page).

entries.title: EIA-923 Power Plant Operations Report
entries.description: Monthly and annual plant-level data on U.S. electricity generation, fuel consumption, fuel stocks, and fuel receipts and costs, collected through Form EIA-923 and its predecessors (EIA-906/920).
entries.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-923
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. Page shows the monthly release of October 23, 2026 (August 2026 data), with the next due end of November 2026, and the annual final 2025 release of September 14, 2026. EIA publications are public domain (EIA Copyrights and Reuse page).

entries.title: EIA Open Data (API v2 and bulk files)
entries.description: The U.S. Energy Information Administration's programmatic access point to its published energy statistics — petroleum, natural gas, coal, electricity, renewables, nuclear, state energy data, and forecasts — through API v2 and bulk download files.

access.auth_note: Free API key via registration on the Open Data page; bulk files need no key.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, state, plant level depending on dataset); some international series

entries.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Open Data
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. Page offers API key registration under the API Terms of Service and describes the bulk files. EIA's Copyrights and Reuse page (https://www.eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php) states its publications are in the public domain. Cadence is event because series update on their own release schedules.

entries.title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO)
entries.description: EIA's monthly 18–24 month forecasts of U.S. and global energy supply, demand, and prices — oil, petroleum products, natural gas, electricity, coal, and renewables — with full data tables.

access.auth_note: Web tables are open; API access goes through EIA Open Data, which needs a free key.

coverage.temporal: recent history plus the forecast horizon

entries.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. Page shows "Release Date: October 6, 2026 | Forecast Completed: October 1, 2026 | Next Release Date: November 10, 2026" and links to all tables and figures. API availability is through EIA's Open Data service (see eia-open-data). EIA publications are public domain.

entries.title: EIA State Energy Data System (SEDS)
entries.description: EIA's consistent state-level estimates of energy production, consumption, prices, and expenditures by source and sector for every U.S. state, back to 1960.
entries.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. Page lists "1960-2024 estimates" and a 2025 update release schedule, plus an October 2023 methodology change for noncombustible renewables. EIA publications are public domain.

entries.title: Ember Yearly Electricity Data
entries.description: Ember's open global dataset of annual electricity generation, capacity, demand, imports, and power-sector emissions by country and fuel, assembled from national and multilateral statistics.
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The site footer states "All content is released under a Creative Commons Attribution Licence (CC-BY-4.0)". The Data menu lists an API alongside the datasets. Ember is a UK think tank (a Community Interest Company) whose data is built on national and multilateral sources. It is cataloged for its open license and coverage; for a primary source, prefer the national statistics agencies. The 2000 start year and the API's auth terms come from Ember's usual description and were not checked here; a steward should confirm them.

entries.title: EPA Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database (eGRID)
entries.description: EPA's comprehensive source of environmental characteristics of almost all U.S. electric power generation — emissions, emission rates, net generation, and resource mix — at plant, state, and grid-subregion level.

coverage.spatial: United States (plant, state, balancing authority, eGRID subregion)
coverage.temporal: data years back to 1996 (latest edition eGRID2023)

entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (page "Last updated on September 21, 2026"). The detailed-data page (https://www.epa.gov/egrid/detailed-data) lists eGRID2023, released 1/15/2025 with revisions on 1/17/2025 and 6/12/2025, as an xlsx download with a PDF technical guide. Editions now come out roughly yearly but not on a fixed schedule, so cadence is irregular. The 1996 start year comes from EPA's historical editions and should be confirmed by a steward.

entries.title: Eurostat Energy Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU energy statistics — energy balances, supply and consumption by fuel, prices, and renewables shares — harmonised across EU member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page shows the Energy database with selected datasets and the data navigation tree. Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) licenses its content under CC BY 4.0. Cadence varies by table (monthly to annual), so it is recorded as irregular for the collection. API and bulk access go through Eurostat's general dissemination services.

entries.title: IAEA Power Reactor Information System (PRIS)
entries.description: The IAEA's database of the world's nuclear power reactors: units in operation, under construction, suspended and in decommissioning, with design characteristics, net capacity, electricity production and operating performance, collected since 1969 through data providers nominated by Member States.

coverage.spatial: global (IAEA Member States with nuclear power)

entries.license: IAEA Terms of Use — content may be reused "for use in commercial and non-commercial products or services" with acknowledgement of the IAEA; databases are "provided free of charge for educational and informational use" (not a named open licence; see notes)
entries.attribution: International Atomic Energy Agency, Power Reactor Information System (PRIS)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). https://pris.iaea.org/ answers a 302 to https://pris-stats.iaea.org (page title "PRIS Analytics"), which is cataloged. The page says "The Power Reactor Information System (PRIS) is the world's authoritative source of official data and statistics on nuclear power development and performance. It contains information collected by the IAEA since 1969". It shows 417 reactors in operation in 31 countries (379 611 MW(e) net), 78 under construction, 21 in suspended operation, and "Electricity Produced (2025) 2 635 TWh", with 2026 editions of the RDS-2 and OPEX reports derived from PRIS. There is a Data Browser (https://pris-stats.iaea.org/data-browser); I did not find or test an export function, so no formats or bulk method are listed.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the PRIS footer's "Terms of Use" link (https://nucleus.iaea.org/Pages/Others/Disclaimer.aspx) says under "Copyright": "Content may be adapted, translated, copied, printed and downloaded for private study, research and teaching purposes, and for use in commercial and non-commercial products or services, provided that appropriate acknowledgement of the IAEA as the source is given". Under "Digital Repositories and Databases": "The data in the IAEA digital repositories and databases is provided free of charge for educational and informational use", and it may include third-party data. The two clauses differ on commercial use, so both are quoted; a steward may want IAEA to clarify.

entries.title: JODI-Gas World Database
entries.description: Monthly natural gas production, trade, consumption, and stock data for participating economies, compiled by the Joint Organisations Data Initiative from national submissions to its partner organisations — the gas counterpart to JODI-Oil.
entries.publisher: Joint Organisations Data Initiative (JODI), coordinated by the International Energy Forum (IEF)

access.auth_note: CSV downloads are open; the JODI REST API requires a free JODI website account.

entries.license: unverified — downloads are offered free of charge; no data license is stated on the JODI site
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The data downloads page (https://www.jodidata.org/gas/database/data-downloads.aspx) says complete series "from January 2009 to one month-old can be downloaded, for free, in a beta version of .csv format". It also says JODI-Gas is available through the JODI REST API, which needs a free JODI website account. The API's json format is assumed. No license is stated, matching the jodi-oil-world-database entry.

entries.title: JODI-Oil World Database
entries.description: Monthly oil production, trade, refinery, demand, and stock data for over 100 economies, compiled by the Joint Organisations Data Initiative from national submissions to its partner organisations.
entries.publisher: Joint Organisations Data Initiative (JODI), coordinated by the International Energy Forum (IEF)
entries.license: unverified — downloads are offered free of charge; no data license is stated on the JODI site
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: jodidata.org returned HTTP 200. The data downloads page (https://www.jodidata.org/oil/database/data-downloads.aspx) offers the complete series "from January 2002 to one month-old" for free in .ivt (Beyond 20/20) and .csv. The partners page lists IEF, APEC, Eurostat, GECF, IEA, OLADE, OPEC, and UNSD. The canonical_url /oil/ is the section root; scripts/check_links.py reported it ok (HTTP 200). "Over 100 economies" comes from JODI's usual description and was not checked against the participant list. JODI-Gas is a separate database and deserves its own entry.

entries.title: National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB)
entries.description: A serially complete collection of hourly and half-hourly solar irradiance (global horizontal, direct normal, diffuse horizontal) and meteorological data for the United States and a growing set of international locations, with typical meteorological year (TMY) files, from the national laboratory formerly called NREL.
entries.publisher: National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, formerly the National Renewable Energy Laboratory), for the U.S. Department of Energy

access.auth_note: The NSRDB Viewer download needs no key; the NSRDB API on developer.nlr.gov needs a free API key.

coverage.spatial: United States and selected international locations (western hemisphere from GOES satellites; India and others)

entries.license: NLR data notice — free use and copying, provided the notice is kept and DOE/NLR/Alliance is credited (NLR Disclaimer, "Data and Software"; not a named open licence; NLR is contractor-operated, so not treated as US Gov work)
entries.attribution: National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB), U.S. Department of Energy / National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The issue's https://nsrdb.nrel.gov/ did not resolve: curl got a proxy 502 and WebFetch got ENOTFOUND, as for every *.nrel.gov host this session. The Department of Energy renamed NREL the National Laboratory of the Rockies on 1 December 2025, and the site now answers at https://nsrdb.nlr.gov/, which is cataloged. Whether nrel.gov redirects there on an open network was not established. The page reads "NSRDB 2025 GOES satellite data for the western hemisphere is now available" and "NSRDB data is publicly available at no cost. The data can be accessed via the NSRDB Viewer Application" (https://maps.nlr.gov/nsrdb-viewer/). The U.S. data page lists "Years Covered 1998-2025". A keyless call to the NSRDB API on developer.nlr.gov returned 403 "API_KEY_MISSING". Not checked: download formats, the HSDS/cloud access.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the NLR Disclaimer (https://www.nlr.gov/disclaimer, last updated Dec. 10, 2025), "Data and Software" section: "The user is granted the right, without any fee or cost, to use or copy the Data, provided that this entire notice appears in all copies of the Data. Further, the user agrees to credit the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)/NLR/ALLIANCE in any publication that results from the use of the Data." The DOE/NLR/Alliance names may not be used to endorse products without permission. NLR is "operated for the U.S. Department of Energy by the Alliance for Energy Innovation, LLC", so the data is not a federal employee work.

entries.title: World Bank Energy & Mining Indicators (World Development Indicators)
entries.description: Cross-country energy indicators — electricity access, consumption, renewable share, and energy imports — compiled by the World Bank as part of its World Development Indicators database.
entries.notes: Verified reachable this session (HTTP 200). IEA and IRENA — the other obvious international energy-statistics bodies — both returned bot-challenge pages (Cloudflare / Azure WAF) on direct fetch this session, the same class of block tracked for BLS/SEC in almanac-template#2. Worth a headless-verified follow-up entry once that fix lands, rather than skipping them. Seeded as this vertical's first international (non-US) source per operator request to seed the new verticals international-first.
